assessments.zone: Rural villages of Kakwa (Adi) away from the South Sudan border, Adja, Laybo/Kaliko-Omi interior and Biringi/Ndo areas
assessments.evidence: No reported armed-group control in these rural areas as of 2026; South Sudanese incursions concern the immediate border strip. Mbororo herders reported in Ndo secteur (Bholi, June 2026) were expelled by local authorities. Assigned to state police/customary authorities by default.

assessments.zone: Villages within ~9 km of the South Sudan border: Kakwa chefferie (Adi HZ: Azu, Rumu, Liku, Kongoroko, northern Gaki/Rikazu/Etukaliri health areas, e.g. Nyangbara, Ranyaka, Bazi, Kendrio, Leiko, Karagba, Nyeite) and Kaliko-Omi (Lipku)
assessments.evidence: Since Dec 2025 repeated incursions by armed men from South Sudan (reported as SPLA-IO 'AIO' groups of 100+ and SSPDF soldiers) in Kakwa border groupements (Rumu, Agoroba, Ulendere, Arile) and Kaliko-Omi: looting of cattle, killings, sexual violence and abductions (70+ people 11-12 May 2026, per OCHA), causing preventive displacement into the bush. Raiders withdraw across the border and no foreign force is reported holding villages; local leaders say the FARDC presence on the border is 'very minimal'. Army assigned as main state force with low confidence; status contested because of recurrent raids.

assessments.zone: Main towns: Ingbokolo (Kakwa chefferie trading centre near Uganda border), Gombe, Atsinia, Eriku, Mobiri, Laybo
assessments.evidence: Ingbokolo and the other towns host chefferie/territorial administration, PNC and state services (CNPR post reopened Aug 2026, Ebola prevention campaigns Aug 2026); no armed group holds them. Insecurity is criminal (armed robberies in Aru/Ariwara, July 2026) and state forces are accused of illegal roadblocks and extortion in Kakwa (Oct 2025), confirming state forces as the coercive power. South Sudanese incursions hit border villages, not these towns.

assessments.zone: Aru town (territorial seat, Uganda border post; all neighbourhoods: Aru Cité, Ania, Katanga, Bakhita, Buta, Eru Yofenyiri, Leri, Araba)
assessments.evidence: Aru is the territorial capital and a major Uganda border crossing with territorial administration, PNC, DGM/customs and an FARDC presence; no armed-group control of the town is known. No web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, sites blocked), so this is a default-presence assessment.

assessments.zone: Rural villages of Aru health zone / Aru secteur (Obang'a, Obhiaku, Ezoo, Adaru, Vis-à-vis, Opirivu, Yaba, Ongoyi, Ekanga, Essebi etc.)
assessments.evidence: No reported armed-group activity or territorial control in Aru secteur; the Ituri armed conflicts (CODECO, ADF, Zaïre) are concentrated in Djugu, Irumu and Mambasa far to the south. Assigned to state police by default. No web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, sites blocked), so this is a default-presence assessment.

assessments.zone: Ariwara town (commercial hub; neighbourhoods Ariwara, Ovutsiri, Dema, Angiria, Apaa, Kuku)
assessments.evidence: Ariwara is a large cross-border trading town near Uganda and South Sudan with permanent state police and services; no armed-group control is known. No web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, sites blocked), so this is a default-presence assessment.

assessments.zone: Rural villages of Ariwara, Adja, Laybo and Adi health zones in the unit (Ariko, Nderi, Edipi, Kuno, Abedju, Donzu, Rogale, Lea, Kikia, Essoko etc.), up to the South Sudan border
assessments.evidence: No reported armed-group territorial control; FARDC hold positions along the Uganda/South Sudan borders against cross-border incursions and criminality, while villages are administered by chiefs and state police. Assigned to PNC by default. No web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, sites blocked), so this is a default-presence assessment.

units.CD5409-aru-2: Aru territory part 2 (Kakwa chefferie/Adi health zone around Ingbokolo, Adja, Laybo/Kaliko-Omi and Biringi/Ndo areas, northern Ituri on the Uganda and South Sudan borders) is outside the Ituri conflict core (CODECO in Djugu/Mahagi, ADF in Irumu/Mambasa) and no armed group holds territory. Towns (Ingbokolo, Gombe, Atsinia, Eriku, Mobiri, Laybo) are state-held with PNC, territorial administration and some FARDC; state forces are themselves accused of illegal roadblocks and extortion in Kakwa. Since late 2025 the South Sudan border strip of Kakwa (Rumu/Azu/Liku/Kongoroko groupements) and Kaliko-Omi has suffered repeated cross-border incursions by South Sudanese armed men (reported as SPLA-IO 'AIO' rebels and SSPDF soldiers): looting, killings and mass abductions (70+ at Ulendere/Arile, 11-12 May 2026), with preventive displacement and only a thin FARDC presence; these border villages are rated contested/low confidence. Rest of the rural area is state police by default; Mbororo herders reported in Ndo/Biringi in June 2026 were expelled. Reviewed 2026-10-01 with web research.
units.CD5409-aru-1: Aru territory part 1 (Aru and Ariwara health zones, Kakwa/Lugbara/Alur country on the Uganda and South Sudan borders) lies far north of the CODECO conflict in Djugu and of the ADF zone in southern Ituri, and has no known armed-group territorial control. Aru town (territorial seat, border post with Uganda) and the trading hub of Ariwara are assessed as held by state police with FARDC garrisons and border services. Rural villages are assigned to the PNC by default state presence; cross-border criminality and occasional South Sudanese armed spillover near the northern border are handled by FARDC and do not amount to control. NOTE: no web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, sites blocked); all zones are default-presence assessments and should be re-checked.
